move.proposition: A design explanation requires defensible expectations about divine intentions and goodness, but suffering and theological uncertainty undermine those expectations.

components.text: Whether theism predicts fine-tuning without a defensible account of what a good divine designer would intend.
Whether merely identifying agency yields discriminating expectations about the universe an agent would create.
Whether life-permitting conditions specifically confirm design when divine purposes remain uncertain.

response.rationale: The reply identifies an internal predictive tension: skeptical uncertainty about divine purposes also removes the fine-tuning expectation.

charity.alternative: A good creator may broadly favor embodied moral agents without guaranteeing a suffering-free or uniquely optimized universe.
charity.decisiveQualification: That broad intention requires independent defense and may yield only weak, nondiscriminating expectations.
